title: Fubini for coherent colimits over two independent indexing quasicategories
statement:
Use the universes, quasicategories, coherent diagrams, functor categories and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and a containing universe. Let $J,K$ be $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories and $\mathcal C$ a quasicategory in the containing universe admitting all $J$-indexed and all $K$-indexed colimits. For any coherent $H:J\times K\to\mathcal C$, there exist a coherent diagram $L:J\to\mathcal C$ and a transformation $\tau:H\to L\operatorname{pr}_J$ whose restriction to each $\{j\}\times K$ is a colimit cocone of $H(j,-)$. Let $L$ and $\tau$ be any such pair. If $L\to\Delta_J c$ is colimiting, then its composite with $\tau$, $H\to\Delta_{J\times K}c$, is colimiting. Thus the product-indexed colimit exists and the canonical comparison is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{colim}_{(j,k)\in J\times K}H(j,k)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{j\in J}\operatorname{colim}_{k\in K}H(j,k).$$
The same holds in the other order. These comparisons identify the colimit cocones: the leg at $(j,k)$ is the composite of the inner leg at $k$ and outer leg at $j$. They are natural in $H$, compatible with restriction in additional simplicial parameter variables, and include all coherent transformations and higher simplices. Empty $J$ and $K$ are allowed. All functor categories are formed in a universe containing $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng, Corollary 6.10, proof: the unlabelled Fubini step in the product-comma colimit calculation. General coherent-colimit formulation supplied by the agent; no Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Work in one universe containing all the displayed functor simplicial sets; enlarge it again for additional parameters when necessary. Put $D_T=\operatorname{Fun}(T,\mathcal C)$ for $T=J,K,J\times K$. These are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The exponential identity gives a simplicial isomorphism $D_{J\times K}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(J,D_K)$: an $n$-simplex on either side is the same map $J\times K\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$, with the factors rearranged. Its inverse rearranges them back, and every simplicial operator is precomposition in the last factor on both sides. Write $\widehat H:J\to D_K$ for the curried diagram. Under this identity $\Delta_{J\times K}x$ becomes $\Delta_J(\Delta_Kx)$; a map $H\to L\operatorname{pr}_J$ becomes $\widehat H\to\Delta_K L$, where $\Delta_K L$ means postcomposition of $L$ with $\Delta_K:\mathcal C\to D_K$.

proof.text:
For $T=J$ and then $T=K$, every $F\in D_T$ has a colimiting cocone $u_F:F\to\Delta_T c_F$ by the hypotheses. The dual cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says exactly that $v\mapsto\Delta_T(v)\circ u_F$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c_F,x)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{D_T}(F,\Delta_Tx)$ for every $x$. Apply the left-hand dual of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] with $T$ there equal to the functor $\Delta_T$, its source $\mathcal C$, and its target full subcategory all of $D_T$. It supplies a coherent $Q_T:D_T\to\mathcal C$ and $\eta_T:\mathrm{id}_{D_T}\to\Delta_TQ_T$, whose components have this universal property and hence are colimiting. Its dual coherent-diagram clause gives, for every parameter simplicial set $P$, diagrams $B:P\to D_T$, $A:P\to\mathcal C$, the equivalence
$$\Phi_{T,P}:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathcal C)}(Q_TB,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(P,D_T)}(B,\Delta_TA),\quad v\longmapsto(\Delta_Tv)\circ(\eta_TB).$$
This is the cited lemma's dual formula, with its stated evaluation and restriction compatibilities. Only the original $T$-shaped colimits were used: no $P$-shaped colimits or smallness of mapping spaces in $\mathcal U$ is required.

proof.text: Take $L_0=Q_K\widehat H$ and let $\tau_0$ be the uncurrying of $\eta_K\widehat H$. The restriction of $\tau_0$ at $j$ is $\eta_{K,\widehat H(j)}$, so step 2 and the dual cone criterion make it colimiting. This proves the demanded existence of the coherent inner-colimit diagram and its cocone. Notice that an unrelated selection of objectwise apices was not asserted to be functorial: the universal-arrow assembly produced both the functor and the transformation.

proof.text:
Now use any pair $(L,\tau)$ allowed by the statement, and write $\widehat\tau:\widehat H\to\Delta_K L$ for its currying. The equivalence $\Phi_{K,J}$ with $A=L$, $B=\widehat H$ supplies $a:L_0\to L$ and a homotopy $(\Delta_K a)\circ\eta_K\widehat H\simeq\widehat\tau$. Evaluation, explicitly compatible with $\Phi_{K,J}$, makes $a_j$ a cocone-preserving morphism from the colimit cocone $\eta_{K,\widehat H(j)}$ to the colimit cocone $\tau_j$. Both are initial objects in the same cocone quasicategory. Choose a reverse morphism using initiality; each of their composites is homotopic to the appropriate identity because each initial object's endomorphism space is contractible. Thus $a_j$ is an equivalence. The componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $a$ an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)$. For every $G:J\to\mathcal C$, precomposition by $a$ is an equivalence of mapping spaces by the inverse-homotopy clause of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. Consequently
$$\beta_{\tau,G}:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)}(L,G)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,D_K)}(\widehat H,\Delta_K G),\quad b\longmapsto(\Delta_Kb)\circ\widehat\tau$$
is an equivalence: associativity and the displayed homotopy identify it with $\Phi_{K,J}\circ(-\circ a)$. This verifies universality for the prescribed $\tau$, not merely for the chosen assembled $\tau_0$.

proof.text:
Let $\lambda:L\to\Delta_J c$ be any colimiting outer cocone, and let $\sigma:H\to\Delta_{J\times K}c$ be the uncurrying of $(\Delta_K\lambda)\circ\widehat\tau$. Such composition is provided in the functor quasicategory by [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. For every $x\in\mathcal C$, there is a composite equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(c,x)\xrightarrow{\lambda}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)}(L,\Delta_Jx)\xrightarrow{\beta_{\tau,\Delta_Jx}}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,D_K)}(\widehat H,\Delta_J\Delta_Kx)\cong\operatorname{Map}_{D_{J\times K}}(H,\Delta_{J\times K}x).$$
The first map is an equivalence by the dual cone criterion for $\lambda$; the second is step 4; the last is the simplicial isomorphism of step 1. The composite sends $v:c\to x$ to $\Delta_{J\times K}(v)\circ\sigma$: before uncurrying it sends $v$ to $(\Delta_K\Delta_Jv)\circ(\Delta_K\lambda)\circ\widehat\tau$, and associativity gives the formula. The dual cone criterion therefore says that the specified composite cocone $\sigma$ is colimiting. Its leg at $(j,k)$ is $\lambda_j\circ\tau_{j,k}$, since evaluation preserves composition and the exponential identity is factor rearrangement.

proof.text: Apply step 5 to the assembled $L_0$ of step 3 and a $J$-colimit of it, which exists by hypothesis. This proves existence of all $J\times K$-colimits under precisely the stated assumptions. If a product colimit with its cocone has already been chosen, it and this iterated cocone are initial objects of the same cocone category. A morphism between them and a reverse morphism exist by initiality; their composites are identities up to homotopy by contractibility of the endomorphism spaces. Projection to $\mathcal C$ gives the asserted equivalence of apices with its cocone-preserving homotopy. Hence it identifies the specified legs, rather than just yielding an abstract equivalence of objects. The core on these initial cocones is contractible by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], giving uniqueness of the cocone-compatible comparison through all higher homotopies. Interchange $J$ and $K$, using the degreewise transpose $J\times K\cong K\times J$, and repeat steps 1--5. The hypotheses are symmetric, so the other iterated order is colimiting too, with its own composite legs; comparison through the product cocone identifies both orders.

proof.text: To make naturality explicit, step 6 now permits step 2 with $T=J\times K$, giving $Q_{J\times K}$ and its universal cocone $\eta_{J\times K}$. Let $D=D_{J\times K}$ and define $I:D\to\mathcal C$ by currying, postcomposition with $Q_K$, and $Q_J$. The transformations $\eta_K$ and $\eta_J$ give a coherent $s:\mathrm{id}_D\to\Delta_{J\times K}I$: its value at $H$ is the composite cocone of step 5. For precision, first whisker $\eta_K$ by the curried diagrams to get the inner transformation, then whisker $\eta_J$ by $Q_K\widehat H$ and postcompose with $\Delta_K$ to get the outer transformation, then compose in the corresponding functor quasicategory and uncurry. These operations form $s$ on the entire diagram quasicategory. Apply the dual parameter formula for $Q_{J\times K}$ with parameter $P=D$, $B=\mathrm{id}_D$ and $A=I$. The preimage of $s$ is a coherent transformation $e:Q_{J\times K}\to I$, together with a coherent homotopy $(\Delta_{J\times K}e)\circ\eta_{J\times K}\simeq s$. Each $e_H$ is a cocone-compatible comparison between initial cocones as in step 6 and is an equivalence. The componentwise criterion makes $e$ a natural equivalence of functors on $D$. It therefore includes noninvertible coherent transformations between diagrams and all higher simplices. The same construction after transposing factors gives the other-order natural equivalence.

proof.text: All the compatibility claimed for additional simplicial parameters can now be read on these constructions. For a simplicial set $P$ and a parameterized diagram $h:P\to D_{J\times K}$, the comparison is $e h$ and its cocone homotopy is the one in step 7 whiskered by $h$. For $r:P'\to P$, $(e h)r=e(hr)$ as a restriction of the same simplicial map; currying rearranges the factors in $P\times J\times K\times\Delta^n$, so it also commutes with $r$ and every face and degeneracy. The mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] is explicitly compatible with these restrictions. Composites and their coherence are retained by [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]; its boundary lifting and the contractible universal-choice spaces supply the comparisons between choices. These statements do not assert that arbitrary $P$-indexed colimits exist: only diagram functors with parameter $P$ are used. Empty shapes are covered without any separate nonemptiness assumption. If $J=\varnothing$, its colimit and the product colimit are initial objects. If $K=\varnothing$, the assembled inner values are initial; step 4 remains valid, and step 5 computes the colimit of this coherent $J$-diagram as the initial object, even when $J$ is not contractible. The universal-arrow criterion is vacuous if the diagram domain is empty, and the mapping-space equivalences remain valid. In all cases the proof uses just the colimits required in the statement.
